research:
I couldn't load the AAA page or any AAA article directly because the proxy refused every fetch. The figures below come from search-result summaries of AAA and other pages. Several results were dated after October 2, and I ignored them.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the AAA national average for regular gas on October 5, 2026, shown at [gasprices.aaa.com](https://gasprices.aaa.com/). AAA posts a new daily number early in the morning, and resolution is about 07:41 UTC, so the October 5 figure should be the one used.
- 2026-10-02: Choose Energy, using AAA and DOE data, put the national average at about **$4.40** for regular. [chooseenergy](https://www.chooseenergy.com/data-center/cost-of-driving-by-state/)
- 2026-10-01: AAA's weekly update put the national average at **$4.41**, down nearly 7 cents from the week before. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/)
- I couldn't get AAA's exact three-decimal figure for October 2.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The latest level (about $4.40) is roughly 2 cents above the $4.38 threshold, and it has been falling.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-10-01: AAA said September set a record. The average for the month was $4.33, about 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 from 2023. The early-October dip came as crude fell back into the $90s per barrel. [AAA newsroom](https://newsroom.aaa.com/2026/10/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/)
- 2026-09-30: WTI traded near $89 to $90 after falling 3.5% the day before, and Brent was near $103. [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-29/latest-oil-market-news-and-analysis-for-sept-30), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/article/price-of-oil-09-30-2026/)
- 2026-09-29: Brent settled at $102.59 (down 2.6%) and WTI at $89.38 (down 3.5%), as crude exports from the Middle East recovered. [Rio Times](https://www.riotimesonline.com/oil-markets-latam-wednesday-september-30-2026)
- 2026-09-24: The national average peaked at about $4.48, the highest ever for that time of year. AAA's September 2026 news covers this period. [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/2026/09/)
- Background: the Iran war and tension around the Strait of Hormuz have kept crude high. The national average has been above $4 since late July. [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/data-graphics/gas-prices-iran-war-state-national-cost-trump-rcna265835)

## 4. Base rates and trend
- 2026-09-04: about $4.15. 2026-09-24: about $4.48. 2026-10-01: $4.41. 2026-10-02: about $4.40. [chooseenergy](https://www.chooseenergy.com/data-center/cost-of-driving-by-state/), [AAA](https://gasprices.aaa.com/national-average-dips-following-record-setting-september/)
- From September 24 to October 1 the average fell about 1 cent a day. Choose Energy's figure suggests about 1 cent more on October 2.
- To stay at or above $4.38 on October 5, the average can fall at most about 2 cents over 3 days, or roughly 0.7 cents a day. That is a little slower than the recent pace.
- On both sides of a crude move, the national average typically changes about 0 to 3 cents a day. Over 3 days that usually means a move of up to about ±5 to 8 cents. Pump prices react to crude with a delay of several days to two weeks, so the September 29 crude drop was probably still pushing prices down in early October.
- The seasonal switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline (from September 15) usually pushes prices down in early October. I'm inferring this from general seasonal patterns, not a specific source.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi has a weekly AAA gas market for the week of October 5 ([kxaaagasw-26oct05](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxaaagasw/us-gas-price-up/kxaaagasw-26oct05)), but I couldn't see what it was pricing before October 2.
- I found no Polymarket or Manifold market and no expert point forecast for October 5.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-10-02: Crude trading on Friday, plus any news about Iran or Hormuz over the weekend. A sharp crude rally would slow the fall at the pump only after a lag, so it would have little effect by October 5.
- 2026-10-03 to 10-05: AAA's daily updates, with the October 5 morning figure deciding the question.
- Risks that could push prices up: a Middle East escalation, such as tanker attacks or the Hormuz disruptions seen later in the month, or an unplanned refinery outage.
